why: ADOPTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R2), was `declined`/`absent` on the reason that the overload "buys nothing when there is one caller shape" -- a preference, not an RTOS constraint. `nros_node::IntoNodeOptions<'a>` (re-exported as `nros::IntoNodeOptions` and in the prelude) is implemented for `&'a str` and `NodeOptions<'a>`, with rclrs's `into_node_options` and `namespace`; `Executor::create_node` and `NodeContext::create_node` take `impl IntoNodeOptions`, so `executor.create_node("talker")` and `create_node("talker".namespace("/robot"))` read as rclrs. ENVELOPE: rclrs's other builder steps (`arguments`, `use_global_arguments`, `enable_rosout`, `start_parameter_services`, `clock_type`, `clock_qos`) configure what RFC-0045 fixes at build time, so they are absent and a call is a compile error. On the executor, the options' defaults (namespace `/`, domain 0) mean the executor's own namespace and session, as a bare name always did. PRIOR ROW: the trait letting rclrs accept `&str` or a full options struct wherever a node is created. Our `NodeOptions` is one concrete type taken by value; the ergonomic overload needs a blanket impl that buys nothing when there is one caller shape.

envelope.text: configure what is fixed at build time here
